Flight engine and aircraft sources

This simulator runs JSBSim 1.2.4, compiled to WebAssembly, in a dedicated worker. The runtime is unchanged from @0x62/jsbsim-wasm 1.2.4-beta.4. That bridge is an independent project, not an official JSBSim browser release.

JSBSim is licensed under LGPL-2.1; the JavaScript SDK is under the MIT license. Download the corresponding source and build instructions. The separate engine files can be replaced with a compatible rebuild.

The aircraft is an experimental C172S approximation derived from the upstream C172R model, which already specifies a 180 hp engine. We added 114 lb at the empty-aircraft centre of gravity, bringing initial gross weight to 2,550 lb. Aerodynamic tables, propulsion and inertia parameters otherwise remain upstream values. View the modified aircraft XML.

The model uses estimated aerodynamic data and is not manufacturer validated. Its previous custom-engine handbook calibration does not apply to this JSBSim model. Automatic mixture follows atmospheric pressure; flaps are controllable and native ground handling is enabled on a flat plane.

The selectable F-15 Eagle model comes from the same JSBSim revision, with two F100-PW-229 engines. We corrected two aileron scale inputs to consume the model’s left-aileron-pos-norm kinematic output; its original input referred to an unbound property. Effective lateral control moment is multiplied by 3.2 in Flight Lab to increase roll authority; this is an approximate tuning change, not manufacturer-validated data. Other aerodynamic data remains upstream. Gear is retractable and native ground handling is enabled; F-15 flaps are not modeled. The speedbrake remains stowed. The shared cockpit and chase-view geometry are simplified visualizations, not an authentic F-15 cockpit or systems simulation.

The 737 cockpit option uses the generic JSBSim 737 aircraft with two CFM56 engines. This is not a calibrated 737-800 model. Its external telnet/QTJSBSIM input ports were removed; app controls use the JSBSim property API. Flight data otherwise remains upstream. The aircraft XML identifies GPL licensing; GNU GPL text is included. Uploaded cockpit model credits and changes.
